correctness.rationale: The upper derivative bound freezes a base minimizer maximizing the stress pairing; the lower bound follows perturbed minimizers and uses strict-BV compactness, weak-* stress continuity, and the explicit quadratic perimeter remainder. Applying the formula to the opposite direction gives the left derivative. Stress rigidity then makes two-sided differentiability equivalent to uniqueness up to complement.

originality.rationale: The motivating preprint supplies the fixed-set perimeter variation, boundary stresses, compactness, and stress rigidity, but does not state a derivative formula for the optimized profile or a metric kink criterion. Targeted literature and SCOPE searches found no matching statement; the classical general envelope-theorem principle is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The theorem converts boundary stress into a complete first-order metric sensitivity law and makes noncomplementary multiplicity exactly detectable as a directional kink of the isoperimetric profile, with a global exponential stability bound on the same metric slice.
